holding_summary: APTEL sets aside a MERC order reopening settled coal shortfall compensation issues for Adani Power's Tiroda plant, directing fresh tariff orders in six weeks using previously fixed parameters.
why_it_matters: If a state regulator reopens a change in law compensation it already settled, cite this ruling to argue fresh hearings on those parameters are impermissible absent a genuinely new event.

case_name: Central Consumer Protection Authority, Suo Motu Proceedings Against Xboom
citation: Case No. CCPA-2/15/2026-CCPA, order dated 17 September 2026
holding_summary: CCPA fines Xboom Rs 10 lakh for advertising anti-drone devices without licence disclosures, rejecting its claim that cart-free, enquiry-only listings fall outside advertising rules.
why_it_matters: Before listing a licence-dependent product online without a purchase option, treat the listing as an advertisement and disclose the applicable approvals on the listing itself.

case_name: Naresh Kumar v. State of U.P. and Another
citation: Allahabad High Court, Criminal Revision, order dated 18 September 2026
holding_summary: Allahabad High Court upholds a doubled maintenance order against a retired Additional District Judge, finding he concealed his pension revision and rejecting his second-marriage defence.
why_it_matters: In a maintenance enhancement proceeding, disclose pension, salary or other income revisions fully; concealment discovered later weighs heavily against the paying spouse.

case_name: [Homebuyers] v. Sai Enterprises and Super Construction
citation: MahaRERA, non-compliance/execution application, order dated 8 October 2026 (underlying order dated 31 October 2025)
holding_summary: MahaRERA imposes a Rs 10 lakh Section 63 penalty on two developers for ignoring a 2025 order to allot a flat, after they sold the project's remaining inventory to third parties.
why_it_matters: If a promoter ignores a MahaRERA allotment or possession order, file a non-compliance application to secure a separate Section 63 penalty plus recovery warrants for amounts already due.

case_name: ACC Limited v. State of Karnataka and Others
citation: Karnataka High Court, order dated 8 September 2026
holding_summary: Karnataka High Court quashes a Rs 482.69 crore mining penalty on ACC over its Kalaburagi lease, holding the lease stood extended to 2030 and rejecting the clinker-to-limestone royalty method.
why_it_matters: If a mining department treats a pre-2015 lease as lapsed for want of a fresh deed, check whether Section 8A(5) of the MMDR Act statutorily extends it before conceding the lapse.

case_name: Kavitha Kuruganti v. PepsiCo India Holdings Private Limited
holding_summary: Supreme Court holds PepsiCo's FL 2027 potato registration cannot be revoked merely for suing farmers, but confirms sued farmers can still invoke the Section 39(1)(iv) saved-seed defence.
why_it_matters: A farmer sued for infringing a registered plant variety should plead Section 39(1)(iv) of the PPV&FR Act as a specific, provable defence, not assume the registration's validity decides the case.

case_name: Tata Capital Financial Services Limited (now Tata Capital Limited) v. Neel Motors LLP and Others
citation: Commercial Arbitration Petition No. 620 of 2021
holding_summary: Bombay High Court allows Tata Capital to pursue arbitration against Neel Motors LLP's personal guarantors, holding the 2026 IBC amendment removing their moratorium protection covers applications already pending.
why_it_matters: Before relying on a guarantor's pending Section 95 insolvency application to resist recovery, check whether the 2026 amendment to Sections 96 and 124 of the IBC has already removed that protection.

case_name: State Bank of India v. Garden Court Distilleries Private Limited and Another
citation: Company Appeal (AT) (Ins) Nos. 1138 and 1145 of 2026
court: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, Principal Bench, New Delhi
holding_summary: NCLAT sets aside an NCLT order that applied a later IBBI amendment to Garden Court Distilleries' going-concern sale, holding the regulations on the liquidation order's own date govern, and remands within two weeks.
why_it_matters: In a going-concern liquidation sale, fix the applicable IBBI regulations by the date of the Section 33 liquidation order itself, not the date a sale implementation application is finally decided.

case_name: High Point Supply Company LLC v. Agati Healthcare Private Limited
citation: Commercial First Appeal No. 15 of 2026 (COMFA/15/2026)
holding_summary: Bombay High Court restores a distributor's suit against Agati Healthcare, holding the Section 12A mediation-urgency exception needs only a limited threshold check, not a merits or delay test.
why_it_matters: When pleading the Section 12A urgent relief exception to mediation, frame the continuing breach clearly on the plaint's face; delay alone should not disqualify it at this threshold stage.

case_name: In Re: Flipkart Internet Private Limited (Cyclosinone Herbicide proceedings)
citation: Central Consumer Protection Authority, order dated 22 September 2026
holding_summary: CCPA fines Flipkart Rs 10 lakh (Amazon equally, JioMart Rs 5 lakh) for advertising an unregistered 'Cyclosinone' herbicide, rejecting the marketplace-intermediary defence.
why_it_matters: Marketplaces carrying agro-chemical listings should verify registration under the Insecticides Act before a product goes live, not after a trade body complains.

case_name: Mahinder and Others v. Puran Singh
holding_summary: SC rules in Mahinder v. Puran Singh that the Section 22 HSA right of co-heirs to buy out a stranger's purchased share extends to agricultural land, distinguishing Atam Prakash.
why_it_matters: Before buying an undivided share of inherited agricultural land from one co-heir, check whether the other Class I heirs have been given notice of their Section 22 pre-emption right.

case_name: National Highways Authority of India v. The Louis Berger Group Inc. (JV with COWI A/S)
citation: O.M.P. (COMM) 351/2023, decided 3 August 2026
holding_summary: Delhi HC severs and sets aside the future O&M component of an arbitral award against NHAI in the Chambal bridge consultancy dispute, upholding the principal payment claim.
why_it_matters: When seeking relief in arbitration against a public authority for a continuing service contract, confine the claim to amounts already due rather than a forward valuation of future performance.

case_name: Manas Shelters Private Limited v. Vivek Madhavlal Pittie
citation: Interim Application No. 4450 of 2026 in Commercial Suit No. 344 of 2015, order dated 2 September 2026
holding_summary: Bombay HC rejects Manas Shelters' summary judgment bid in its Rs 31.10 crore Tardeo redevelopment suit against Vivek Pittie, ordering a full trial on termination and loss.
why_it_matters: Before applying for summary judgment on a large damages claim, assess whether questions of readiness to perform, causation and quantum can genuinely be resolved without oral evidence.

case_name: Dharmendra Hansraj Kotak & Ors. v. State of Delhi & Anr.
citation: Delhi High Court, Section 482 CrPC petition, order dated 6 August 2026
holding_summary: Delhi HC quashes the 2015 Maggi lead prosecution against Nestle distributors, holding that CFTRI's later court-ordered retest eroded the original Food Analyst findings.
why_it_matters: If a court-supervised referral test later contradicts the Food Analyst report underlying a pending prosecution, consider a Section 482 CrPC petition rather than contesting only at trial.

case_name: Hari Dutta Sharma v. State of U.P. & Ors.
holding_summary: SC holds a financier's night-time, no-notice repossession of a hypothecated truck violated Articles 14 and 21, ordering loan closure, a refund with interest, and RBI enforcement.
why_it_matters: Before authorising a vehicle repossession, confirm the contractual notice period has run and that no agent will act by force or outside daylight hours.

case_name: Parshvadhara Complex ABCD Co-operative Housing Society v. M/s. Parshwanath Developers & Ors.
citation: Appeal No. AT006000000345557 of 2024, MahaREAT, arising from Complaint No. CC006000000020890 of 2022 before the MahaRERA Authority
holding_summary: MahaREAT orders a Thane developer to pull down an entire unauthorised wing, holding that a later planning sanction cannot replace allottees' own informed consent under MOFA and RERA.
why_it_matters: A statutory building sanction obtained after flats are sold does not satisfy RERA's consent requirement; promoters need specific, informed allottee consent for each additional structure.

case_name: National Highways Authority of India v. Bareilly Highways Project Limited
citation: Arbitral award disclosed via official NHAI statement issued 27 July 2026; exact date of signing of the award not disclosed in public reporting
court: Arbitral Tribunal (ad hoc, constituted under the concession agreement)
holding_summary: A tribunal slashes a Rs 3,177 crore claim against NHAI over the terminated Bareilly-Sitapur toll project to about Rs 46 crore, finding the delays were concurrent rather than NHAI's alone.
why_it_matters: In BOT termination arbitrations, a concurrent-delay finding can wipe out the bulk of a concessionaire's claim regardless of its headline value; delay attribution usually decides the quantum.

case_name: Petitioner (husband) & Anr. v. State of Kerala & Anr. (parties not named in available reporting)
citation: 2026 LiveLaw (Ker) 512; Crl.M.C. No. 5128 of 2026
holding_summary: Kerala HC refuses to quash a domestic violence complaint filed years after separation, holding the PWDV Act sets no limitation period and that delay alone cannot end the case at the threshold.
why_it_matters: A long gap before filing a Section 12 PWDV Act complaint is not by itself a ground for quashing; courts treat delay and claims of retaliatory motive as questions for trial, not threshold dismissal.

case_name: HDFC Bank Ltd. v. Kishore K. Mehta (Dead) Thr. LRs
holding_summary: Supreme Court rules a pre-2016 DRT recovery certificate cannot be used to launch a personal insolvency notice against a borrower, dismissing HDFC Bank's appeal over a 2004 certificate.
why_it_matters: Check the date of any recovery certificate before relying on it for an insolvency notice: only certificates issued after the 2016 RDB Act amendment carry decree-like status for that purpose.

case_name: All India Trade Union Congress & Others v. State of Karnataka & Others
citation: Writ petitions filed by AITUC and others, Karnataka High Court, interim order dated 18-19 September 2026, staying circulars dated 29 July, 10 August and 28 August 2026
holding_summary: Karnataka HC stays three government circulars that tried to defer a minimum wage hike for contract and outsourced workers, while a separate employer challenge to the wage notification itself is sent to a Division Bench.
why_it_matters: A circular cannot override an unstayed statutory wage notification; apply the revised Karnataka minimum wage rates unless a court has specifically stayed the notification itself.

case_name: Hinduja National Power Corporation Limited & Anr. v. Regional Director, Southeastern Region & Anr.
citation: Company Appeal (AT)(CH) No. 88 of 2026, NCLAT Chennai Bench, order dated 25 September 2026
court: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, Chennai Bench
holding_summary: NCLAT revives the HNPCL-GOCL merger scheme, holding that NCLT Amravati's rejection over the appointed date and financial discrepancies came too early, before shareholders and creditors had even voted.
why_it_matters: If a tribunal rejects a merger at first motion over a long appointed-date gap, check whether that gap tracks time spent awaiting SEBI or exchange observations.

case_name: D v. S
citation: 2026 INSC 1043, decided 23 September 2026
holding_summary: Supreme Court allows a mother to relocate her children to the UK and denies the father custody while his POCSO prosecution is pending, striking down the Delhi High Court's remarks on the FIR's credibility.
why_it_matters: In a custody case involving a pending POCSO prosecution, do not ask the family court to assess the FIR's merits; custody can be withheld on the bare fact of the pending case.

case_name: Hotel Alankar v. State of Maharashtra
citation: 2026 BHC KOL 8650 (DB)
holding_summary: Bombay HC's Kolhapur Bench holds that an FSSAI licence suspension cannot continue once re-inspection shows the establishment has fixed the problem, rejecting its use as an open-ended penalty.
why_it_matters: After a Section 32(3) suspension, get a prompt re-inspection and use a strong score to press for revocation; absent a specific, ongoing risk, the authority cannot keep it running.

case_name: Urmila Kumari Kadam v. Y.B. Builders Pvt. Ltd. & Nimai Developers
citation: Appeal No. 696 of 2026, Haryana REAT, order dated 31 August 2026, reported as 2026 LLBiz REAT (HR) 62
holding_summary: Haryana REAT rejects a homebuyer's delay compensation claim, holding that a possession offer made before the contractual due date is valid even where no Builder Buyer Agreement was signed.
why_it_matters: When assessing a delayed-possession claim, compare the offer date against the fixed due date first; the gap to the final Occupation Certificate may not be decisive.

case_name: Rekha Saxena and Anr. v. Roman Catholic Diocese Allahabad Pvt. Ltd. Thru Director General, The Bishop
citation: (2026) 09 AHC CK 4243, Allahabad High Court, Lucknow Bench, appeal under Order XLIII Rule 1(r) CPC from an order of the Civil Judge (Senior Division), Raebareli
holding_summary: Allahabad HC's Lucknow Bench grants an injunction to a woman in 38 years of possession, holding that a decree cancelling the sale deed behind her possession does not by itself authorise her eviction.
why_it_matters: Before acting on a decree that cancels a sale deed, check whether it also directs eviction; if not, you cannot dispossess the occupant without a separate order.

case_name: Anjaniputra Ispat Ltd. v. IAG Company Ltd.
citation: Company Appeal (AT) No. 39 of 2026 with connected Company Appeal (AT)(Ins) No. 1874 of 2025, NCLAT Principal Bench, decided September 2026
court: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, Principal Bench, New Delhi
holding_summary: NCLAT dismisses an appeal as time-barred after the appellant converted a late Section 61 IBC appeal into a fresh Section 421 Companies Act appeal rather than amending the existing filing.
why_it_matters: If a tribunal allows converting a Section 61 IBC appeal into a Section 421 appeal, file it as an amendment, not a fresh appeal, or the limitation clock resets against you.

case_name: Deyzeel Aggarwal v. InterGlobe Aviation Ltd.
citation: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-I (North District), Delhi, order reported 16 September 2026
court: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-I (North District), Delhi
holding_summary: Delhi consumer commission holds IndiGo liable for marking a passenger a no-show after he arrived ahead of the delayed departure time the airline itself had texted him, rejecting its Conditions of Carriage defence.
why_it_matters: If an airline reschedules your flight and still denies boarding, keep that SMS or email; a commission can treat it as overriding the Conditions of Carriage on check-in timing.

case_name: Commissioner of Service Tax, Mumbai v. M/s Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd. & Ors.
citation: Civil Appeal Nos. 2471-2473 of 2015, 2026 INSC 723, decided 20 July 2026
holding_summary: Supreme Court revives a Rs 16.68 crore service tax demand against BPCL and HPCL, holding their CNG retail distribution for Mahanagar Gas was taxable Business Auxiliary Service, not a sale on their own account.
why_it_matters: Before treating a distribution arrangement as your own sale, check who fixes the price, holds title and bears commercial risk; that allocation decides the service tax position.

case_name: Maternal Grandparents v. Biological Father (parties not named in available reporting)
citation: D.B. Civil Misc. Appeal, Rajasthan High Court, Jodhpur Bench, decided on or about 6-7 October 2026 (case number not available in the reporting reviewed)
holding_summary: Rajasthan High Court sets aside a Family Court order giving a father custody, holds the child's settled bond with his grandparents outweighs the father's bare legal right, and orders only phased access.
why_it_matters: In custody disputes against an absentee legal guardian, lead with evidence of the child's existing bond and the disruption a sudden transfer would cause, not just the guardian's weaker paper claim.

case_name: Haryana Power Purchase Centre v. Siwana Solar Power Projects Ltd. (arising from proceedings before the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission)
citation: Appeal before APTEL against HERC's order in Petition No. 78 of 2025, decided 18 September 2026 (APTEL appeal number not available in the reporting reviewed)
holding_summary: APTEL sets aside an HERC order that had revived a solar developer's claim to a higher tariff, holding the claim was already finally decided by an unappealed 2024 order and could not be reopened through a fresh petition.
why_it_matters: Treat an unappealed regulatory order as final; a fresh petition seeking the same relief on a repackaged theory will not survive appeal even if the regulator first grants it.

case_name: State of Gujarat v. Chimanbhai Bhanubhai Chaudhari & Ors.
citation: R/CR.A/918/2008, 2026:GUJHC:40381, Gujarat High Court, decided 17 June 2026
holding_summary: Gujarat High Court confirms an acquittal over kaju katli coated in aluminium foil, holding there was no proof the foil was injurious to health and that the sampling procedure was flawed.
why_it_matters: In adulteration prosecutions, press on both fronts: demand proof the substance is actually harmful, and scrutinise whether the sample bottle and collection procedure met basic protocol.

case_name: Ramamurthy v. Rajendran
citation: O.P. No. 69 of 2012, with connected A.Nos. 3416, 3417, 3419 of 2026 & 4268 of 2023, Madras High Court, decided 24 September 2026
holding_summary: Madras High Court rejects a Letters of Administration petition by MGR's brother's heirs, holding MGR's 1987 will, probated in 1992, already covers the asset and leaves no room for intestacy.
why_it_matters: Before filing a Letters of Administration petition against a probated estate, confirm the asset actually falls outside the will's terms; probate forecloses intestacy claims asset by asset.

case_name: Aroha Labs Pte. Ltd. v. Prem Dharmani & Ors.
citation: AP.IM. No. 4 of 2026, Karnataka High Court, decided on or about early August 2026 (reported 3 August 2026)
holding_summary: Karnataka High Court partly allows a Section 9 petition by a Singapore company despite its SIAC arbitration being seated abroad, holding a foreign seat alone does not oust interim relief absent an express exclusion.
why_it_matters: If a cross-border arbitration agreement is meant to exclude Indian courts even for interim relief, say so expressly; a foreign seat alone will not achieve that exclusion.

case_name: Polycab India Limited v. Asier Metals (arising from Asier Metals' Section 9 petition against Polycab India Limited)
citation: Appeal against NCLT Ahmedabad's order in C.P.(IB) No. 273/9/AHM/2026, NCLAT Principal Bench, New Delhi, stay order dated 9 October 2026 (appeal number not available in the reporting reviewed)
court: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal, Principal Bench, New Delhi
holding_summary: NCLAT stays an NCLT order admitting Polycab India into insolvency over a roughly ₹2.79 crore claim by Asier Metals, conditional on a full deposit, appeal listed for 26 October 2026.
why_it_matters: Document a provisional-billing or reconciliation-pending dispute before the NCLT at the admission stage; a later appellate stay will not reverse exchange-level consequences already triggered.

case_name: Ramegowdu Mahendra v. Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax
citation: W.P. No. 32056 of 2026, Madras High Court, decided 20 August 2026
holding_summary: Madras High Court holds income tax reassessment cannot ride piggyback on a GST adjudication order, though it declines to quash the notice itself on the Revenue's assurance of an independent reassessment.
why_it_matters: Where a reassessment notice leans on a GST order, raise the independence objection now and save it for the final reassessment order, since the notice alone is unlikely to be quashed on that ground.

case_name: IFCI Limited v. Hotel Mythri & Anr.
citation: OP(C) No. 2569 of 2026, Kerala High Court, decided 15 September 2026
holding_summary: Kerala High Court holds a lessee who lost a SARFAESI challenge before the DRT cannot relitigate the same grievance through a fresh civil suit, the claim being barred by Section 35 and res judicata.
why_it_matters: If a lessee or occupant has already lost a Section 17 SARFAESI challenge before the DRT, raise Section 35 and res judicata immediately against any fresh civil suit covering the same ground.

case_name: Omaxe Limited & Ors. v. Securities and Exchange Board of India
citation: (2026) 09 SEBI CK 4384, Securities Appellate Tribunal, order dated 1 September 2026, dismissing the appeal against SEBI's order dated 30 July 2024
holding_summary: SAT dismisses Omaxe's appeal against SEBI's two-year market ban over alleged ₹647 crore round-tripping, calling the deals fraudulent 'make believe' dealings and rejecting leniency on penalties.
why_it_matters: When defending related-party deals against a round-tripping claim, focus on real commercial substance; SAT looks past documentary form once a PFUTP violation appears evident on the transactions.

case_name: BRD Finance Ltd. v. Santhosh P. & Anr.
citation: RSA No. 194 of 2026, decided 10 August 2026
holding_summary: Kerala High Court voids a decade of litigation after finding a Munsiff Court kept deciding a Rs 3.47 lakh suit on merits years after it lost jurisdiction to a newly designated Commercial Court.
why_it_matters: Check pending recovery suits against the state's Commercial Courts notification and threshold; a decree from the wrong forum is void and challengeable at any stage.

case_name: Alpro Industries & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors.
citation: W.P.(C) 12818/2026, decided 30 September 2026
holding_summary: Delhi High Court rejects a constitutional challenge to the 2018 Commercial Courts Amendment's cut-off date, confirming pre-May 2018 suits stay outside the Commercial Courts regime however small the claim.
why_it_matters: Stop filing transfer applications to move pre-3 May 2018 suits into Commercial Courts on the lowered threshold; Section 19's prospective application is now upheld as constitutional.

case_name: U.P. State Highways Authority v. M/s Abhijeet Meerut Karnal Toll Road Limited
citation: Section 37 Appeal No. 41 of 2025, 2026 LLBiz HC (ALL) 58, decided 23 July 2026
holding_summary: Allahabad High Court upholds a PPP arbitral award's breach finding against a state highways authority but strikes down its Rs 157.57 crore loss-of-profits component for resting on a financial model alone.
why_it_matters: In PPP termination arbitrations, back any loss-of-profits claim with evidence beyond the financial model, such as cost records, or risk losing that head of damages on a Section 37 appeal.

case_name: Petitioner (landowner) v. National Highways Authority of India & State of Bihar (parties not fully named in available reporting)
citation: CWJC No. 10512 of 2026, decided 28 July 2026
holding_summary: Patna High Court orders NHAI to redo a blank highway land notice and pay a landowner ₹5,000 after both NHAI and the State admitted the original communication named no land, date or reference number.
why_it_matters: Before acting on a highway land notice, check it names a specific parcel and carries a reference number and date; one missing these basics can be treated as no notice at all.

case_name: ANI Media Private Limited v. RSY News & Anr.
citation: CS(COMM) 1018/2024, 2026:DHC:8749, decided 29 September 2026
holding_summary: Delhi High Court permanently restrains RSY News and directs Google to block URLs after finding it copied ten of ANI's twelve disputed videos wholesale, rejecting a fair dealing defence RSY News never even raised.
why_it_matters: Before reusing a rival's footage under the reporting-current-events exception, add independent reporting of your own; reproducing the original wholesale will not qualify as fair dealing.

case_name: Sun Pharma Laboratories Ltd. v. Finecure Pharmaceuticals Ltd. & Ors.
citation: FAO(OS)(COMM), decided 1 July 2026
holding_summary: Delhi High Court Division Bench reverses a 2023 refusal of interim injunction, restraining Finecure's Pantopacid products as deceptively similar to Sun Pharma's registered Pantocid mark.
why_it_matters: A validity challenge to a rival's registered mark must displace the Section 31(1) presumption of validity, not just raise doubt about it, to defeat an interim injunction application.

case_name: Angurbala Mondal v. State of West Bengal & Ors.
citation: W.P.A. 22494 of 2026, 2026 LiveLaw (Cal) 393, decided 14 September 2026
holding_summary: Calcutta High Court rules police cannot decide whether a neighbour's dairy farm is illegal or a health hazard, directing the complainant to the West Bengal Pollution Control Board instead.
why_it_matters: Facing police pressure over your dairy or livestock operation's waste practices, insist the complaint go to the State Pollution Control Board; police have no authority here.

case_name: Shamshid Ahmed & Ors. v. Union Territory, Chandigarh & Ors.
citation: CWP (number not available in reporting reviewed), decided on or about 24 September 2026
holding_summary: Punjab and Haryana High Court upholds demolition of a decades-old fish and poultry operation in Chandigarh's periphery, rejecting the operators' Article 21 livelihood defence and their claim to a rehabilitation policy.
why_it_matters: Do not rely on years of running a livelihood business on unauthorised land as a defence to demolition; Article 21 protects earning a living lawfully, not an illegal structure that funds it.

case_name: Eco Green Buildtech Ltd. v. Vikartan Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd.
citation: OMP (ENF.) (COMM.) 193/2023 & EX.APPL. (OS) 1449/2023, CNR No. DLHC010405902023, decided 10 September 2026
holding_summary: Delhi High Court sets aside two arbitral awards worth crores after finding the tribunal relied on a party's conciliation-stage statements once settlement talks collapsed, breaching settlement confidentiality.
why_it_matters: If a tribunal's award relies on anything said or conceded during failed conciliation within the arbitration, raise it as a confidentiality-based Section 34 ground; it can void the award entirely.

case_name: Bhawani Construction Pvt. Ltd. v. Odisha Real Estate Regulatory Authority
citation: OREAT Appeal No. 22 of 2026, 2026 LLBiz REAT (OD) 45, order dated 12 June 2026
holding_summary: Odisha Real Estate Appellate Tribunal quashes a ₹7 lakh ex parte RERA penalty after the regulator admitted it sent the show-cause notice to an address that was never the developer's own.
why_it_matters: Before accepting an ex parte RERA penalty as final, verify notice went to your actual registered or operating address; defective service can void the order for breach of natural justice.

case_name: Gaurav Jain & Anr. v. Joint Commissioner (Appeals-II), CGST Delhi Zone & Anr.
citation: W.P.(C) 8414/2026; reported as 2026:DHC:6124-DB, Delhi High Court
holding_summary: The petitioners were issued a show cause notice dated 25 June 2025 under Section 122(1A) of the CGST Act proposing only a personal penalty, with the penalty confirmed by an Order-in-Original dated 16 December 2025. A Division Bench held that the right of appeal vests on the date the show cause notice is issued, not on the date of the Order-in-Original or the appeal filing, so the 10% pre-deposit requirement for penalty-only appeals (introduced by the amendment to the proviso to Section 107(6) of the CGST Act with effect from 1 October 2025) could not be applied to a notice issued before that date.
why_it_matters: Gives a taxpayer facing a penalty-only GST order a concrete basis to resist the 10% pre-deposit demand whenever the underlying show cause notice predates 1 October 2025, regardless of when the final order or appeal itself was filed.

case_name: Chattar Singh v. Executive Engineer, HPSEBL & Ors.
citation: CWP No. 8209 of 2026, Himachal Pradesh High Court, decided 16 September 2026
holding_summary: The petitioner's daily-wage engagement with HPSEBL's Rajgarh Division was terminated with effect from 12 March 1997; a Labour Court award dated 27 November 2024 found the termination illegal and ordered reinstatement with seniority and continuity of service, but refused back wages. The High Court set aside the denial of back wages, holding that once a workman pleads he remained unemployed after termination, the burden shifts to the employer to prove he was gainfully employed during the intervening period, which HPSEBL had not done, and directed HPSEBL to pay 50% back wages with up-to-date interest within six weeks.
why_it_matters: Reinforces that an employer cannot avoid back wages merely because a long gap has passed since termination — once the workman pleads non-employment, the employer must affirmatively prove gainful employment elsewhere or pay up.

case_name: RBI enforcement action against Punjab National Bank (currency chest penalties)
citation: Reserve Bank of India penalty orders dated 9 and 11 September 2026 under RBI's Master Directions on Currency Chests; disclosed by PNB on 14 October 2026
holding_summary: RBI imposed four separate monetary penalties on Punjab National Bank totalling about Rs 8.6 lakh for non-compliance with its Master Directions on currency chest operations: Rs 2,91,750 on 9 September 2026, and Rs 1,33,800, Rs 1,34,600 and Rs 2,99,600 on 11 September 2026. PNB disclosed the penalties to the stock exchanges only on 14 October 2026, explaining that the amounts had been directly debited from its account with RBI and were identified during periodic reconciliation, which caused the delay in disclosure.
why_it_matters: Another entry in a recurring pattern of RBI penalties on PNB for currency chest lapses through 2026, and a reminder that such penalties can be debited directly from a bank's RBI account well before the bank discloses them to the market.

case_name: Amba Grains Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. v. Amit Agrawal, RP of Mastana Foods Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.
citation: NCLAT, Principal Bench, New Delhi, decision reported 14 October 2026 (connected appeals including CA (AT) (Ins) No. 4257 of 2025 in CP(IB) No. 630 of 2019)
court: National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), Principal Bench, New Delhi
holding_summary: Mastana Foods Pvt. Ltd. had been admitted into CIRP in September 2019 on an SBI petition, and NCLT Delhi later approved a Rs. 135.39 crore resolution plan from a consortium of HR Commercials Pvt. Ltd. and Crown Steels. A rival bidder, Amba Grains Pvt. Ltd., and the corporate debtor's suspended directors filed five connected appeals challenging the plan's approval, raising the conduct of the e-bidding process, a post-bid clarification sought on treatment of Haryana VAT/Excise dues, and the Committee of Creditors' refusal to consider a higher revised offer from Amba Grains. NCLAT dismissed all five appeals, holding that its review of a CoC-approved plan is confined to compliance with Section 30(2) of the IBC and does not extend to re-appraising the CoC's commercial wisdom, and separately held that a plan clause using the word 'may' made formation of a special purpose vehicle optional rather than mandatory for the successful resolution applicant.
why_it_matters: A disappointed bidder cannot use an appeal against plan approval to re-litigate the CoC's commercial choice between competing offers or to challenge discretionary (as opposed to mandatory) implementation steps in the approved plan — NCLAT's review stays confined to the statutory compliance checklist in Section 30(2).

case_name: SEBI (Settlement of Administrative and Civil Proceedings) Regulations, 2026
citation: SEBI Gazette notification, issued on or about 6-7 October 2026, coming into force 7 November 2026
court: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
holding_summary: SEBI notified a new Settlement of Administrative and Civil Proceedings Regulations, 2026, which will repeal and replace the existing 2018 settlement framework with effect from 7 November 2026, subject to transitional and savings provisions for applications already pending under the 2018 regulations. Reported changes include a formula-based settlement-amount calculation, fast-track treatment for smaller matters, and minimum settlement amounts (reported as roughly Rs. 3 lakh for first-time applicants and Rs. 7 lakh for others), alongside stricter debarment consequences for non-compliance with settlement terms.
why_it_matters: Entities currently negotiating or planning a SEBI settlement should factor in the new formula-based amount calculation and stricter debarment terms taking effect from 7 November 2026, and confirm which framework (2018 or 2026) will govern a pending or contemplated application under the transitional provisions.

case_name: In Re: Adani Enterprises Ltd., Adani Green Energy Ltd., Adani Total Gas Ltd., AWL Agri Business Ltd. & Adani Energy Solutions Ltd. (SEBI settlement)
citation: SEBI settlement order, proceedings closed 22 September 2026
court: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
holding_summary: SEBI's adjudication proceedings against five Adani group companies, arising from its examination of related-party-transaction disclosure and audit-certification issues flagged after the Hindenburg Research report, were closed by settlement after the companies paid a combined Rs. 1.5 crore (Adani Enterprises Rs. 76.05 lakh for alleged non-disclosure of certain related-party transactions and audit/limited-review reports signed by a firm without a valid Peer Review Certificate; Adani Green Energy Rs. 45.50 lakh; and Adani Total Gas, AWL Agri Business and Adani Energy Solutions Rs. 9.75 lakh each over reports signed by firms lacking a valid Peer Review Certificate). The companies paid without admitting or denying the findings, and SEBI expressly reserved its right to act further if any submission is later found false or a settlement condition is breached.
why_it_matters: A reminder that an issuer's related-party-transaction disclosures and the Peer Review Certificate status of the firm signing its audit or limited-review reports are both independently checked by SEBI, and that a lapse on either front can draw a separate adjudication and settlement even where no restatement or fraud finding is involved.

case_name: Percept Talent Management Pvt. Ltd. & Percept D'Mark (India) Pvt. Ltd. v. Sourav Ganguly
citation: Calcutta High Court Division Bench judgment dated 16 April 2026 (Justices Debangsu Basak and Md. Shabbar Rashidi), Section 37 appeal dismissed; Supreme Court subsequently dismissed Percept's SLP (bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana)
court: Calcutta High Court (Supreme Court dismissed the SLP against it)
holding_summary: The Supreme Court dismissed Percept's special leave petition challenging the Calcutta High Court's dismissal of its Section 37 appeal, leaving intact a 2018 arbitral award of Rs. 14.49 crore plus 12% annual interest (from 21 November 2007) and Rs. 50 lakh in costs in favour of former cricketer Sourav Ganguly. The High Court had held Percept lost its right to terminate its 2003 player-representation agreement by waiting too long to exercise it and by continuing to act as Ganguly's agent afterward, and separately upheld the tribunal's finding that Ganguly's Kolkata Knight Riders earnings fell outside the parties' revenue-sharing clause.
why_it_matters: A further example of the narrow scope for interference with an arbitral award under Section 37/Article 136, and a reminder that a contractual termination right can be lost by delay and continued conduct inconsistent with having terminated, independent of the merits of the underlying dispute.

case_name: Andavar Transport v. Deputy State Tax Officer
citation: W.P. Nos. 21226 & 21227 of 2026, Madras High Court, order dated 22 June 2026
holding_summary: A goods transporter faced two separate GST assessment orders (dated 26 April 2024 and 13 August 2024) under Section 73 for the same tax period, 2019-20, despite having reversed the disputed input tax credit from its electronic credit ledger under the first order. Justice C. Senthilkumar Ramamoorthy, with the department's counsel not disputing that both orders covered the same issue, quashed the duplicate order and remanded the matter for fresh adjudication, directing the department to grant a hearing and pass a fresh order within three months.
why_it_matters: Continues a consistent Madras High Court line that two GST orders covering the same tax period and the same alleged default cannot both stand — a taxpayer facing a second, overlapping assessment for a period already covered by an earlier order has a straightforward quashing-and-remand remedy.

case_name: Tetra Technologies Inc. v. Union of India
citation: W.P.(C)-IPD 33/2024, Delhi High Court, order dated October 2026
holding_summary: The Patent Office had treated Tetra Technologies' national-phase patent application as abandoned under Section 21(1) of the Patents Act, 1970 after it did not respond to a First Examination Report said to have been e-mailed to its agent in October 2021; the applicant said neither it nor its agent ever received that e-mail and learned of the abandonment only in April 2023 while checking the application's status online. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav held that a bare record of dispatch of a system-generated e-mail, without proof the e-mail was actually delivered, cannot by itself establish abandonment, since abandonment requires a conscious act or manifest intention on the applicant's part. The Court revived the application, directed the Patent Office to re-send the First Examination Report to the applicant's agent at both postal and e-mail addresses within a week, and granted eight weeks thereafter to respond.
why_it_matters: Gives applicants a concrete precedent to challenge a deemed-abandonment where the Patent Office cannot prove actual delivery of a system-generated FER e-mail, rather than merely dispatch — useful wherever a lapsed response deadline is blamed on a missed e-mail.

case_name: Bhadrashree Steel and Power Limited v. State of Maharashtra
citation: Writ Petition No. 1094 of 2022, Bombay High Court, order uploaded 15 October 2026
holding_summary: Bhadrashree Steel & Power had bought land and a building for about Rs. 8.03 crore (part of a roughly Rs. 13.01 crore total bid) as the successful bidder in an e-auction held by the liquidator of Harneshwar Agro Products Power and Yeast (India) Ltd. under the IBC; the stamp authorities valued the property far higher (first at Rs. 41.96 crore, later revised to Rs. 35.70 crore) under the Annual Statement of Rates and demanded stamp duty on that basis. A Division Bench of Justices Bharati Dangre and Manjusha Deshpande rejected the State's argument that the NCLT is not a 'civil court' for the purposes of Article 16, Schedule I of the Maharashtra Stamp Act, 1958, holding that an NCLT acting as adjudicating authority under the IBC falls within that term; finding the e-auction (with 16 interested bidders) transparent and free of any sign of deliberate undervaluation, the Court directed that stamp duty be levied on the actual auction value of Rs. 8.03 crore and that the sale documents be registered accordingly.
why_it_matters: Gives purchasers at NCLT-supervised liquidation auctions in Maharashtra a clear basis to resist stamp duty demands pegged to Ready Reckoner/ASR valuations where the auction itself was transparent and competitive, rather than the (often much higher) government guidance value.
